title: Ultimate Ghosts 'n Goblins
subtitle: Arthur returns to another hostile kingdom
summary: Ultimate Ghosts 'n Goblins is Tose and Capcom's PSP action-platform game, first released in Japan on 3 August 2006. Arthur again fights through demons and traps, with three-dimensional scenery surrounding a largely side-on route. Series creator Tokuro Fujiwara returned to lead the project. The familiar image remains a knight whose armour can disappear after an encounter goes wrong, leaving him vulnerable in his underwear. New systems change how that danger is managed, giving the handheld game another way to balance the series' demanding action with a longer journey through its stages.
body: Ultimate Ghosts 'n Goblins is Tose and Capcom's PSP action-platform game, first released in Japan on 3 August 2006. Arthur again fights through demons and traps, with three-dimensional scenery surrounding a largely side-on route. Series creator Tokuro Fujiwara returned to lead the project. The familiar image remains a knight whose armour can disappear after an encounter goes wrong, leaving him vulnerable in his underwear. New systems change how that danger is managed, giving the handheld game another way to balance the series' demanding action with a longer journey through its stages.

Standard mode gives Arthur several lives and allows revival at the point of defeat while those lives remain. Improved armour can also withstand more than one hit, changing the immediate cost of an error. The player still has to read enemy movement and commit to jumps carefully, because losing the last protection makes the next contact dangerous. Different weapons and abilities provide alternatives, while exploration gives reasons to look beyond the most direct path. The new allowances make room to learn a hostile section without removing the need to understand why it defeated Arthur.

Fujiwara's return connects the PSP release to the series' early arcade identity while the new presentation brings its monsters and environments into three dimensions. Masaya Tsunemoto and Kazuhiro Kotani supplied the music. North American and European editions followed shortly after Japan in 2006. The game is a new chapter rather than a simple transfer of an older release, changing survival rules and adding ways to explore. Its central appeal remains the same difficult bargain: Arthur is capable enough to win, but the player must learn to use that capability in places designed to punish carelessness.

Survive the mistake, then decide where to search
A creator revisits a demanding formula
